title: Smoothness of fixed schemes of torus actions on smooth affine schemes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $T$ be an affine group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$ such that $T_{\bar k}\simeq(\mathbf G_m)^r$ for an algebraic closure $\bar k/k$ and an integer $r\geq0$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $X$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $a:T\times_kX\to X$ be a morphism satisfying the group-action associativity and identity laws, with product as in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define the fixed subfunctor by $$X^T(A)=\{x\in X(A):a(t,x_{A\prime})=x_{A\prime}\text{ for every commutative }A\text{-algebra }A\prime\text{ and every }t\in T(A\prime)\}.$$ If a closed subscheme $F\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] represents this subfunctor, then $F$ is smooth over $k$.

source.place: Theorem 13.1, printed p.254, with proof through Theorem 13.7, printed p.256; tori are linearly reductive (opening sentence of Chapter 13, and Theorem 12.30). This is the general fixed-scheme smoothness input, not Corollary 13.10 restated.

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $F=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$ using the given closed immersion. A quotient of a finite-type $k$-algebra is finite type; it is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], since a field is Noetherian. The same holds after any field extension. The fixed-functor description commutes with field extension: for a $K$-algebra $R$, an $R$-algebra $R'$ is already a $K$-algebra, and the universal quantifier over $R'$ and $t\in T(R')$ is identical before and after scalar extension. Thus $F_K$ represents $(X_K)^{T_K}$, with its closed immersion obtained by tensoring the quotient $B\twoheadrightarrow B/I$.

source.place: Theorem 13.1, reduction by extension of the base field; elementary affine base-change check

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-large-algclosed-jacobson] to $F_{\bar k}$ to choose an algebraically closed extension $K/\bar k$ for which $F_K$ is Jacobson and every closed point has residue field $K$. Now $T_K\simeq(\mathbf G_m)^r$. Field extensions are flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat]. Since $X$ is locally finitely presented, [lem-sfb-scheme-lfp-smooth-flat-base-change] implies that $X_K$ is smooth at every point; these smooth open neighbourhoods cover $X_K$, so $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] says that every local ring of $X_K$ is regular. We work over $K$ through step 7.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 13.6 and Theorem 13.7, printed p.256

proof.text: Fix a closed point $x\in F_K$, which is $K$-rational. Set $A=\mathcal O_{X_K,x}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $J=(t^*f-f:t\in T_K(K),f\in\mathfrak m)$. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-fixed-local-ideal-jets]: $\mathcal O_{F_K,x}\cong A/J$, and for every $n\geq1$ the finite-dimensional spaces $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ and $V=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ are rational $T_K$-representations with equivariant quotient map. The local ring $A$ is regular by step 2. Put $d=\dim_K V$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 13.6 and Theorem 13.7, printed p.256

proof.text: A finite-dimensional representation of $(\mathbf G_m)^r$ has simultaneous integer weights by repeated application of [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] to its $r$ commuting factors: the weight spaces for the first factor are preserved by every other factor, so decompose each of them for the second factor, and continue. Equivariant maps preserve each simultaneous weight space. Choose a weight basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of $V$, numbering its nonzero weights first, say $1\leq i\leq s$. For a fixed $n\geq1$ choose any preimage of each $v_i$ in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ and take its component of weight $\chi_i$, the weight of $v_i$. Weight preservation shows that this component still maps to $v_i$. Denote it $w_i$ and choose a lift $u_i\in\mathfrak m$. This supplies an equivariant linear section on $V$, with no assumption that the full local ring is a rational representation.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 13.6 and Theorem 13.7, printed p.256

proof.text: The classes $w_i$ generate $A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ as a $K$-algebra. Indeed, since they lift a basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, replace an element of $\mathfrak m$ by its linear expression in the $u_i$ modulo $\mathfrak m^2$; replace the factors of each residual product in the same way, increasing the residual degree at each stage. After degree $n$ the remainder vanishes. Let $L_n$ be the ideal generated by $w_1,\ldots,w_s$. Each nonzero weight $\chi_i$ takes a value different from $1$ at some $t\in(K^\times)^r$: vary a coordinate with nonzero exponent, using that a nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots and $K$ is infinite. Then $t^*w_i-w_i=(\chi_i(t)-1)w_i$, so $L_n$ lies in the image of $J$. Conversely the quotient by $L_n$ is generated by the images of the weight-zero $w_i$ and scalars, all fixed by $T_K(K)$, so every difference vanishes there. Thus the image of $J$ is exactly $L_n$, or $J+\mathfrak m^{n+1}=(u_1,\ldots,u_s)+\mathfrak m^{n+1}$.

source.place: Lemma 13.6, last paragraph: explicit truncated-polynomial calculation of the difference ideal

proof.text: The integer $s$ is fixed by the weights of $V$, independently of $n$. For every $n\geq1$ the lifts $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ have basis classes in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, and step 5 supplies the required ideal equality. Apply [lem-sfb-regular-quotient-parameter-approximation] to $A$, $J$ and $s$. It gives regularity of $A/J$, hence of $\mathcal O_{F_K,x}$. This includes $s=0$ and $s=d$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 13.6 and Theorem 13.7, printed p.256

proof.text: At the closed point $x$ of $F_K$, the residue field is $K$ and is therefore finite separable over $K$. Apply [lem-sfb-regular-separable-affine-smooth-neighbourhood] with the whole affine scheme $F_K$ to get a smooth open neighbourhood of $x$. The largest smooth open $W\subseteq F_K$ exists by [lem-sfb-space-maximal-smooth-open] (schemes are a special case). It contains every closed point by the preceding argument. Its closed complement must be empty, since the closed points of $F_K$ are dense in every closed subset by the choice in step 2. Thus $F_K$ is smooth over $K$, including when it is empty.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 13.6 and Theorem 13.7, printed p.256

proof.text: The field extension $K/k$ gives a flat surjection of spectra by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat, lem-pc-field-extension-surjective]. Its base change $F_K\to F$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. For any $y\in F$, choose $y_K$ above it. The morphism $F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally finitely presented by step 1, so [lem-sfb-scheme-lfp-smooth-flat-base-change] transfers smoothness at $y_K$ to smoothness at $y$. These smooth open neighbourhoods cover $F$; [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] yields smoothness of $F/k$.

source.place: Theorem 13.1, printed p.256, descent after the algebraically closed-field proof
